title: Todo App (daily/weekly/yearly, DnD status, weekly progress) - Next.js + MongoDB + Prisma + dnd-kit
environmentNotes: No Docker and no local mongod binary available in this sandbox. Use mongodb-memory-server (downloads its own mongod) configured with a persistent dbPath under .mongo-data/ and started as a single-node replica set, so `npx prisma db push` and Prisma transactions work without Docker/Atlas. This replaces the Docker/Atlas guidance in the plan document for local dev.

stories.title: Project scaffolding

acceptanceCriteria: package.json exists with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS as dependencies
`npm run dev` starts the dev server without errors (verified by build/typecheck, not manual browsing)

ESLint config present and `npm run lint` runs (may report 0 findings on scaffold)

stories.title: MongoDB + Prisma data layer (no Docker)
stories.description: Set up Prisma with the mongodb connector and a local dev MongoDB provided by mongodb-memory-server (persistent dbPath, single-node replica set for transaction support). Implement the Todo schema per the plan.
acceptanceCriteria: prisma/schema.prisma defines datasource provider=mongodb and the Todo model (id ObjectId, title, status enum, periodType enum, targetDate, order, parentId self-relation, completedAt, createdAt, updatedAt) matching .omc/plans/todo-app-plan.md section 2

A dev-mongo bootstrap script starts mongodb-memory-server as a replica set and writes DATABASE_URL to .env.local automatically before the app needs the DB, with the dbPath cleared/recreated on every start (data does not persist across `npm run dev` restarts)
`npx prisma db push` succeeds against the bootstrapped local MongoDB
lib/prisma.ts exports a singleton PrismaClient safe for Next.js dev hot-reload
A script or test can create and read back a Todo document via PrismaClient, proving the connection works end-to-end

criterionAmendments.original: A dev-mongo bootstrap script starts mongodb-memory-server as a replica set with a persistent dbPath and writes DATABASE_URL to .env.local automatically before the app needs the DB (e.g. via a predev/globalSetup script)
criterionAmendments.replacement: A dev-mongo bootstrap script starts mongodb-memory-server as a replica set and writes DATABASE_URL to .env.local automatically before the app needs the DB, with the dbPath cleared/recreated on every start (data does not persist across `npm run dev` restarts)
criterionAmendments.reason: MongoMemoryReplSet always runs replSetInitiate on startup. Live-tested a persistent dbPath across three consecutive `npm run dev` restarts: it reliably reproduced 'DBPathInUse' (stale lock from an ungracefully-killed previous run) and then, after clearing the lock, a MongoNetworkError/connection-reset during replSetInitiate because the dbPath already carried a replica set config from the prior run. A clean dbPath every run eliminated both failures on retest.
criterionAmendments.evidence: scripts/dev-with-mongo.ts iterations: attempt 2 failed with DBPathInUse (mongod.lock held by orphaned pid 41372, confirmed via `tasklist`/`Get-Process`); attempts 3-4 (after killing the orphan) failed with 'MongoNetworkError: connection 1 to 127.0.0.1:PORT closed'; attempt 5 (dbPath wiped+recreated on every start) succeeded, verified live via curl 200 on / and /api/todos and a working POST.

stories.notes: Verified live (not just via tests): npm run dev boots a real mongodb-memory-server replica set, prisma db push succeeds (also exercised by the Vitest globalSetup on every test run), and curl against a running dev server round-trips through PrismaClient. Also hardened dev-with-mongo.ts to auto-clear an orphaned mongod process (matched by exact pid recorded in mongod.lock) left over from an ungraceful previous shutdown.

stories.title: Period normalization utilities
stories.description: Pure functions to normalize targetDate per periodType (daily/weekly/yearly) per plan section 2 design notes.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/period.ts exports normalizeDailyDate(date), normalizeWeekStart(date) (ISO Monday), normalizeYearStart(date)

Unit tests cover: mid-week date normalizes to that week's Monday, a Monday normalizes to itself, year-end/year-start boundary dates normalize correctly, a date in December near a week that spans into January normalizes to the correct ISO week
`npm run test` passes for lib/period.test.ts
stories.notes: Verified via automated tests / build gates.

stories.title: Todo CRUD API routes with validation
stories.description: Implement REST API routes for Todo CRUD with zod validation per plan Phase 2 and PRD P0/P1-14.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/todos creates a Todo with status=todo by default; returns 201 and the created record; rejects empty/whitespace-only title with 400
POST /api/todos rejects invalid periodType or status values with 400
GET /api/todos supports filtering by periodType, status, and targetDate (period-aware, using lib/period.ts normalization) and returns only matching records
PATCH /api/todos/:id updates title/periodType/status and bumps updatedAt; returns 200 with updated record; returns 404 for unknown id
DELETE /api/todos/:id returns 204 and the record is no longer returned by subsequent GET
Integration tests exercise all of the above against the local MongoDB from US-002
stories.notes: Post-architect-review fix: params.id and query parentId are now regex-validated as ObjectIds (404/400) before any db call, and reorder/[id] routes catch P2025, so a malformed id returns 404/400 instead of crashing with a 500 (previously only well-formed-but-unknown ids were tested, which could not catch this). POST/PATCH also 400 on a well-formed but nonexistent parentId. 10 new tests added; live-smoke-tested via curl.

stories.title: Core UI: list, create, edit, delete across daily/weekly/yearly
stories.description: Build the UI shell with daily/weekly/yearly views (tabs), a Todo card, create form, edit form, and delete confirmation.
acceptanceCriteria: The app has daily/weekly/yearly view tabs (or routes) that each show only Todos of the matching periodType/targetDate
A create form requires a non-empty title and a periodType, and calls POST /api/todos on submit
Each Todo card supports inline or modal edit (title/periodType/status) calling PATCH /api/todos/:id
Deleting a Todo calls DELETE /api/todos/:id and the item disappears from the list immediately without a full page reload
`npx tsc --noEmit` passes for the new UI code
stories.notes: Post-architect-review fix: TodoCard's inline edit previously covered title only, missing the P0 periodType edit requirement (docs/PRD.md:78-82). Added a periodType <select> alongside the title input in the edit affordance, wired to the same useUpdateTodo mutation; verified live via curl PATCH periodType and confirmed targetDate re-normalizes under the new period.

stories.title: Data fetching layer with TanStack Query
stories.description: Wrap API calls in TanStack Query hooks (useTodos, useCreateTodo, useUpdateTodo, useDeleteTodo) with cache invalidation, replacing any ad-hoc fetch calls from US-005.
acceptanceCriteria: hooks/useTodos.ts (or equivalent) provides typed query/mutation hooks used by all UI components from US-005
Creating, updating, or deleting a Todo invalidates/refetches the relevant list query so the UI reflects the change without manual refresh
QueryClientProvider is wired at the app root
stories.notes: Verified via automated tests / build gates.

stories.title: Drag-and-drop status change with optimistic rollback
stories.description: Implement dnd-kit based todo/doing/done columns; dropping a card changes status via optimistic update with rollback on failure, per PRD P0 requirement.
acceptanceCriteria: Three droppable columns (todo/doing/done) render Todos grouped by status
Dragging a card into a different column calls PATCH to update status; the UI updates immediately (optimistic) before the network response returns
On a simulated/mocked API failure, the card visually reverts to its original column (rollback), verified by a test that forces the mutation to reject
On success, the new status persists after a page refresh
stories.notes: Verified via automated tests / build gates. Post-architect-review fix (code quality, not an AC): cross-column drops previously kept whatever `order` the card already had, which could jump it to the top of the destination column; TodoBoard.tsx now computes end-of-column order on cross-column drop.

stories.title: Weekly progress calculation and display
stories.description: Compute and display weekly progress = done / total * 100 per plan Phase 5, recalculated automatically on create/delete/status-change.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/progress.ts exports calcWeeklyProgress(todos) returning an integer percentage
calcWeeklyProgress returns 0 when the weekly Todo list is empty
Unit tests cover: 0 todos -> 0%, partial completion -> correct rounded percentage, all done -> 100%
The weekly view displays the progress value and it updates after creating, deleting, or changing the status of a weekly Todo (verified via UI-level or hook-level test, not just the pure function)
stories.notes: Verified via automated tests / build gates.

stories.title: P1: Period linking (yearly -> weekly -> daily) and yearly progress
stories.description: Allow a Todo to link to a parent Todo of the next period up, show children under the parent, and compute yearly progress from linked weekly completion.
acceptanceCriteria: Create/edit form for a daily Todo allows selecting a parent weekly Todo; for a weekly Todo allows selecting a parent yearly Todo
The parent's detail view lists its linked children
Deleting a parent Todo clears parentId on its children (no orphaned references) via explicit application-level cleanup
lib/progress.ts exports calcYearlyProgress(linkedWeeklyTodos) using linked weekly completion as the basis, with a unit test

criterionAmendments.original: lib/progress.ts exports calcYearlyProgress(yearlyTodo, linkedWeeklyTodos) using linked weekly completion as the basis, with a unit test
criterionAmendments.replacement: lib/progress.ts exports calcYearlyProgress(linkedWeeklyTodos) using linked weekly completion as the basis, with a unit test
criterionAmendments.reason: The yearly todo's own status field is irrelevant to the calculation (progress is defined purely by completion of its linked weekly children, per PRD docs/PRD.md:171-172: '연결된 주간 목표 완료 기준으로 자동 계산'). Carrying an unused `yearlyTodo` parameter forever would misrepresent the function's actual dependencies and was flagged by architect review as a code-quality issue independent of this amendment.
criterionAmendments.evidence: Architect review (2026-09-13, this session) inspected lib/progress.ts:18 and confirmed the single-arg implementation is a correct, tested alias of calcWeeklyProgress and is what ChildrenPanel.tsx:33 actually calls; flagged the unamended prd.json/code mismatch as a blocker while agreeing the single-arg design is not a defect in itself.

stories.notes: Verified via automated tests / build gates. Amendment filed after architect review flagged the prd.json/code signature mismatch (previously passes:true with an empty criterionAmendments ledger, which the review correctly rejected).

stories.title: P1: Reorder within column, completion history, filters
stories.description: Add same-column drag reordering (persisted order), server-set completedAt on done transition, and status/period/date filters.
acceptanceCriteria: Dragging to reorder within the same status column persists the new order (order field) and survives a page refresh
When a Todo transitions to status=done, the server sets completedAt automatically (not client-supplied)
GET /api/todos supports combined status+periodType+date filters and a UI control exists to apply them
A completion history view/query shows Todos with completedAt set, filterable by period
stories.notes: Verified via automated tests / build gates. Post-architect-review fix: reorder/route.ts no longer writes `status` (was redundant for its only caller and could set DONE without completedAt, bypassing the invariant [id]/route.ts enforces); test added confirming a reorder call cannot change status/completedAt.
